name: Syracuse and the Rocky Necropolis of Pantalica
description: On Sicily's southeastern coast, Syracuse began as the Greek colony of Ortygia, founded by settlers from Corinth in the 8th century BC. Today you can walk from a Greek theatre and a Roman amphitheatre to a cathedral built into a 5th-century BC temple of Athena. Inland, about 23 km northwest, thousands of tombs honeycomb the cliffs of Pantalica's river gorge.
